gen_risks.description: High insecurity and active conflict in project regions may restrict operational access, halt field activities, and prevent service delivery to beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish security SOPs, adopt flexible remote delivery modalities (GEMS, phone monitoring, radio training), partner with local CBOs/NGOs or UN agencies, and maintain CERC activation readiness.
gen_risks.evidence: high insecurity in some of the areas in which project activities will be conducted

gen_risks.description: Lack of pre-existing Financial Management arrangements, staff, software, and auditing procedures in the new PIU creates fiduciary non-compliance and reporting risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified FM specialists prior to project effectiveness, adopt an approved FM procedures manual, acquire accounting software, and engage independent external auditors.
gen_risks.evidence: MFS currently does not have a PIU with FM arrangements in place, including the absence of FM staff, procedures manual, accounting software

gen_risks.description: Administrative approval routines and untrained evaluation committees may result in critical procurement processing delays, stalling project execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate explicit business standards and maximum delays in the PIM, recruit a seasoned procurement specialist, and conduct targeted World Bank procurement training for review committees.
gen_risks.evidence: administrative routines may result in procurement delays, potentially affecting project implementation

gen_risks.description: Limited market participation in conflict-affected regions increases the risk of inflated contract prices, low competition, and supplier collusion.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply World Bank flexible procurement arrangements for fragile situations, engage technical departments early, and utilize STEP for real-time market oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: procurement in fragile areas with few bidders can restrict competition and possibly increase prices and collusion risks

gen_risks.description: Extreme vulnerability of target beneficiaries in conflict settings creates severe exposure to Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Sexual Harassment during project implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an SEA/SH Action Plan, enforce mandatory codes of conduct for project staff and contractors, recruit a GBV specialist, and operate a survivor-centered grievance redress mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: SEA/SH risk is Substantial, reflecting the nature of project activities and the vulnerability of the target population

gen_risks.description: Civil works for 28 food warehouses and 10 regional center rehabilitations could cause localized soil/water pollution and occupational safety hazards for workers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct environmental and social screening for all construction sites, prepare site-specific ESIAs/ESMPs, enforce Labor Management Plans (LMP), and recruit a dedicated environmental specialist.
gen_risks.evidence: water and soil pollution from solid and liquid waste at construction and rehabilitation sites; occupational health and safety of workers

gen_risks.description: Targeting inaccuracies, geographical barriers, or social bias could lead to the exclusion of female-headed households, IDPs, and disabled persons from project benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize community-based pre-identification validated by general assemblies, embed gender-sensitive targeting criteria, deploy mobile intake units, and maintain accessible grievance mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: exclusion from the project’s benefits of certain categories of people such as vulnerable groups including women, youth, people with disabilities

gen_risks.description: Fluid national political dynamics and institutional leadership changes could impair project ownership, policy dialogue, and covenant compliance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a broad multi-stakeholder Steering Committee with statutory and observer members, engage technical secretariats deeply, and maintain continuous policy dialogue.
gen_risks.evidence: the country’s current fluid political situation

gen_risks.description: Recurrent climate shocks such as severe droughts and floods could destroy productive assets of economic inclusion beneficiaries and derail livelihood gains.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate-resilient livelihood diversification and adaptation modules into beneficiary coaching, promote climate-smart agriculture, and maintain CERC funding availability.
gen_risks.evidence: 5 out of 10 Burkinabe in rural areas affected at least once by droughts or irregular rainfall patterns in the previous three years

gen_risks.description: Interconnecting disparate database systems (RSU, WURI ID, Faso Arzeka, CONASUR) presents technical integration risks and potential breaches of personal data privacy.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define standardized interoperability protocols in Year 1, collaborate closely with the Data Protection Authority (CIL) and Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI), and implement strict consent frameworks.
gen_risks.evidence: proper and appropriate application of national data protection and privacy measures and good international practices

gen_risks.description: Severe sectoral fragmentation across dozens of implementing agencies could hinder effective coordination and operational alignment under the national PAMPV flagship program.
gen_risks.mitigation: Operationalize formal inter-ministerial coordination mechanisms, hold regular planning meetings, establish joint operational protocols, and publish unified annual PAMPV work plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Burkina Faso’s social assistance system is highly fragmented, with more than 200 interventions implemented by 50 agencies

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk is assessed to be Substantial. The uncertain political and governance context provides a challenge to long-term development policy. Adaptive social protection systems are still nascent and will require continued political commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The team, guided by the management, will continue its high-level policy dialogue at central and decentralized levels and ensure continuous advocacy and communication.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed to be Substantial. Fiscal space remains constrained by elevated security spending and tighter financing conditions, which increase the risk of reduced budget allocations and delayed counterpart funding for new priorities and reforms, including social protection and the PAMPV. Macroeconomic risks also arise from exogenous factors, including current conflict in the Middle East which can result in a surge in oil prices and put inflationary pressure.
gt_risks.mitigation: Other programs such as the International Monetary Fund program and the World Bank's technical assistance on tax expenditure under the Sustainable Development Finance Policy can help expand fiscal space, partially mitigating these risks.

gt_risks.description: Sector strategy and policies risks are considered to be Substantial. Sectoral strategies and policies remain nascent, and the Government's budget allocation to operationalize the PAMPV remains unclear. Also, sectoral decisions are at times taken abruptly and can heavily affect implementation (for example, the suspension of cash transfers in 2023 led to an increased focus on economic inclusion, and the newly emerged priority of the CONASUR/IDPs led to the revision of the fiche de projet of this project).
gt_risks.mitigation: In parallel with high-level policy dialogue, the project supports strategic communications, adopts an agile approach, and provides technical assistance to promote evidence-based decision-making (with support from SASPP, the Social Protection Response MDTF, and the State and Peacebuilding Fund).

gt_risks.description: Overall fiduciary risks are considered as Substantial, as described in section IV.B and annex 2, based on financial assessment and procurement assessment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project preparation fund (Grant Facility for Project Preparation) has been used not only to prepare mitigation measures to address these risks but will also elevate the project readiness (for example, effectiveness-linked actions including FM and procurement staffing and initiating the procurement packages for the first 18-months' implementation priorities) to improve the project performance.

gt_risks.description: Other risks related to insecurity are rated as High. The deteriorating and volatile security situation—particularly in regions with high poverty, displacement, and food insecurity that are project intervention areas—will likely be an important risk. The project will also address other risks related to protection of personal data: for Component 2 on social registry and interoperability, activities will be guided by the Information System Security Policy (ISSP) document developed by the ANSSI, to ensure confidentiality of households registered in the RSU.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project activities will be adjusted based on the security situation (see annex 3), and the PIU will be also staffed with a security specialist and a security management plan will be developed. To remain engaged, the project will also rely on remote delivery/monitoring, partnering with local representation (NGOs, UN agencies). The ST-RSU will conduct capacity-building activities, including training sessions and awareness campaigns, to strengthen users' ability to manage and protect households' personal data.
